#### 1. ectodermal dysplasia-syndactyly syndrome 1  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.566)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-418990, Reactome:R-HSA-420597)

**Proposed mechanism:** NECTIN1 (HGNC:7770) —DISRUPTS→ Cell-cell adhesion via nectin complex; NECTIN4 (HGNC:37009) —DISRUPTS→ Cell-cell adhesion via nectin complex; Cell-cell adhesion via nectin complex —LEADS_TO→ Cleft lip/palate (HP:0000175); Cell-cell adhesion via nectin complex —LEADS_TO→ Ectodermal dysplasia (HP:0001050); Cell-cell adhesion via nectin complex —LEADS_TO→ Syndactyly (HP:0001159). Loss-of-function mutations in NECTIN1 and NECTIN4 disrupt the nectin-mediated cell-cell adhesion complex, which is essential for craniofacial and limb development, leading to the observed phenotypes of cleft lip/palate, ectodermal dysplasia, and syndactyly.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in NECTIN1 or NECTIN4 with a gain-of-function or dominant-negative effect, or the absence of any variants in these genes in affected individuals, would falsify this hypothesis. Furthermore, if genetic analysis reveals distinct, non-overlapping molecular pathways for each disease that do not converge on cell-cell adhesion or epithelial development, this hypothesis would be falsified. _(variant: None specified)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of NECTIN1 and NECTIN4 in these distinct but overlapping syndromes could reveal therapeutic targets for interventions aimed at improving epithelial integrity and developmental outcomes in both cleft lip/palate and ectodermal dysplasia conditions.
